title: Defining Warehouse Alerts

children:
A warehouse alert can communicate to the user that a certain condition 
 in the warehouse exists and needs attention. You can use warehouse alerts 
 to learn what problem(s) exist in your warehouse and how to resolve them. 
 When a defined alert action occurs, the system can generate a history 
 record (displayed in the Warehouse Alert Viewer), an email message, or both. Also, 
 the system allows you to configure when a warehouse alert should be sent, 
 the email's structure and contents, who should receive it, and the priority 
 that determines when the alert should be addressed (in relation to other 
 alerts).
Defining Interface Validation Error Reference Fields

The "Mail Server" registry value 
 at HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE \SOFTWARE\Manhattan 
 Associates\ILS\ must be set to the name of the machine hosting 
 the mail server software.          If this value is empty or invalid, the 
 system will throw an audit when trying to generate an alert.

Use the Alert 
 Type Field to associate a warehouse process to this alert.         Note that alert types are not configurable in the system. Ask a Manhattan representative if you want to add additional alert types.

Use the Action 
 Field to indicate what you want the system to generate when this 
 alert is triggered.

- Choose "Email" if you want 
 the system to send an email to selected person(s) 
 when this alert is triggered.

- Choose "History" if you want 
 the system to generate a history records when this alert is triggered. 
 You can view this record in the Warehouse Alerts Viewer.

- Choose "History and Email" 
 if you want the system to generate both of these when this alert is triggered.

Use the Priority 
 Field to assign a priority to this alert. This value indicates 
 what order the system will use to process this alert.

Use the Description 
 Field to provide a text description of this alert. This description 
 will appear in this window's record list.

Use the Message 
 Field to provide the text of an alert,         if 
 an email template will not be used. The system uses this message 
 as a default if the system process does not create its own message. Note 
 that all alert processes create their own message except "Inbound 
 Alert" and "Outbound Alert."

Use the Email 
 Title Field to indicate the text of the email's subject line.

Use the Web Description 
 Field to make this alert available for web users. You can use this 
 value to make the description of this alert more understandable to clients 
 using Trading Partner Management to define an alert.

Use the Email 
 Template Field to indicate a pre-made template that you want the 
 system to use to format this email. The template defines the structure 
 and contents of the alerts sent to the email address.

You can use this tab's fields to provide additional criteria that a 
 system record must meet before an alert is triggered. Depending on what 
 alert type you choose, the system may or may not display fields on this 
 tab. If this tab appears, you must provide a value in at least one of 
 its fields.
Using the Interface Error Reference Fields Tab

You can use this tab's fields to view the values that are defined for the twenty interface error reference fields. When you select a different interface process from the Criteria Tab, the system will display the reference fields defined for that process. Note that you cannot change these values from this tab. For more information about interface validation warehouse alerts, see the topic

You will use this tab's fields to identify who should receive an email 
 alert message, as well as the structure and contents of that email. This 
 tab is displayed only if the alert generates emails. You can create multiple 
 records on this tab if you want to send the alert to multiple email accounts.

Right-click on 
 the record list and choose New. The system will open the Warehouse 
 Alert Address Window.

Choose the email 
 address you want to send the email message:

- Select the Email Address 
 Field to define the address that the system will send the alert 
 to (for example, customer@store.com).

- Select the Ship From Email Address 
 Button to send the alert to the email address defined on the Ship 
 From area of the Receipt Screen.

- Select the Vendor Email 
 Address Button to send the alert to the email address defined on 
 the Source area of the Receipt Screen.

- Select the Ship To Email Address 
 Button to send the alert to the email address defined on the Ship 
 To area of the Shipment Screen.

- Select the Customer Email 
 Address Button to send the alert to the email address defined on 
 the Customer area of the Shipment Screen.

- Select the Alternate Email Address 
 Button to send the alert to the email address defined on the General 
 area of the Shipment Screen.

Use the Email 
 Template Field to  indicate 
 a pre-made template that you want the system to use to format this email 
 (if different than the template chosen above). The template defines the 
 structure and contents of the alerts sent to the email address.

Press OK. 
 The system will display the email address in the record list.
